title: MINE-THE-GAP
text:
MINE-THE-GAP is an ERC Consolidator Grant project aimed at scaling monitoring environmental impacts of the mining sector globally. The surge in mining has uncovered a critical gap in our understanding of its environmental and social impacts. Essential indicators, such as precise geographical locations, waste generation, and details of extracted minerals, are surprisingly scant worldwide. MINE-THE-GAP will unlock new avenues in sustainability research, overcoming obstacles caused by the lack of essential geoinformation. It will create the basis for monitoring mining sites globally, which is essential for transparency and for providing mine-level environmental metrics to support decision making.
More details in the MINE-THE-GAP website and data results at MINE-THE-GAP Explore.

Funded by the European Union. Views and opinions expressed are however those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or the European Research Council Executive Agency. title: Dr. Victor Maus
text:
I lead an interdisciplinary research group in data science at WU Vienna University of Economics and Business. With a background in Computational Modelling (MSc) and Earth System Science (PhD), my main research interests are in developing new algorithms and software architectures to meet the scalability needs of planetary-scale geodata. Supported by an ERC Consolidator Grant, I lead the development of distributed high-performance systems that transform massive satellite datasets into actionable insights. A key technical contribution is the TWDTW algorithm, which I develop and maintain as an open-source software on CRAN. By engineering robust, scalable software, my team has enabled global-scale analysis of mineral extraction, revealing previously overlooked environmental footprints worldwide. I am committed to advancing algorithms and software that are robust and reliable to address the complexity of planetary-scale data and the long-term demands of global environmental monitoring.
